newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: DON'T SLAUGHTER SACRED COWS, HINDUS TELL SWISS.
newsitem.headline: DON'T SLAUGHTER SACRED COWS, HINDUS TELL SWISS.

text.p: A Nepal-based Hindu group has urged Switzerland to drop its plan to slaughter 230,000 cattle and offered the sacred beasts a happy home in the Himalayas if Berne gave it the cash earmarked for a "mad cow" cull.

"For us slaughtering cow is more crime than slaughtering anything," the World Hindu Federation wrote in a letter to the Swiss government that was released on Wednesday by Animal Rights Action, an activist group headquartered in Lausanne.
A government spokesman said the cabinet had not received the letter, and an economics ministry spokesman added it was unlikely to comply even if the missive did arrive.

The group was appalled by the Swiss authorities' plan to destroy the animals in an effort to wipe out Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), which many scientists believe could be passed to humans. Switzerland trails only Britain in BSE cases.
Hindus worship cows and revere them with devotion.

The Federation suggested the Swiss government give it the $257 million envisioned for the cull. It wrote: "Please let us know if we can take these cows in Nepal and Swiss Govt. will pay us $257 million to maintain the cows for well?"
